subject: barreleye fish
title: The Deep-Sea Fish With a Transparent Head and Rotating Eyes

scenes.text: This fish can see straight through its own head.
The barreleye lives about two thousand feet down in the ocean, where sunlight never reaches.
Its head is a transparent, fluid-filled dome. Its eyes sit inside, topped with bright green lenses.
Scientists described it in nineteen thirty-nine, but nets destroyed the dome, so it was drawn without one.
Researchers watched the eyes swivel inside the dome: up to spot prey, forward to feed.
A fish a few inches long with a glass head. So yes, it sees through it.

description:
The barreleye is a deep-sea fish with a transparent head and tubular eyes that rotate inside it.
It lives 2,000 to 2,600 feet down, and nets destroyed its fragile dome for decades.
